name: Recombinant protein drugs
how: Recombinant DNA, bacterial/yeast fermentation, protein purification; engineered microbes made to secrete human insulin, growth hormone, EPO
impact: Biologics made this way (human insulin, EPO, clotting factors, antibodies' forerunners) are a third of drug sales and keep tens of millions of diabetics alive.

name: ACE inhibitors
how: Organic synthesis of a peptide-mimic drug; ★ enzyme inhibition of the renin-angiotensin hormone system
impact: Among the most prescribed drugs on earth for high blood pressure and heart failure, taken daily by hundreds of millions.

name: Proton-pump inhibitors
how: Organic synthesis, enteric-coated capsule; ★ acid-activated drug that blocks the stomach's proton pump
impact: Omeprazole and its successors are taken by hundreds of millions for reflux and ulcers and ended most ulcer surgery.

name: Relational database
how: Microchips, hard disk drive, query language (first sold 1979, spread from 1983); ★ set-based tables queried by declarative SQL
impact: Every bank, airline, hospital, shop and website keeps its records in one; the standard way business data works.

name: Local area network (Ethernet)
how: Insulated wire & cable, transceiver chips (standardised 1983 after 1980 spec); ★ collision-detecting shared-medium packet signalling
impact: Wires every office, school, data centre and home router; the wired half of how computers connect.

name: Computer-aided design
how: Personal computer, graphical user interface, computer mouse; vector geometry software
impact: The standard way buildings, machines, chips and products are drawn and engineered worldwide.

name: Conjugate vaccines
how: Vaccination, protein chemistry; ★ sugar antigen chemically linked to a carrier protein so infants' immune systems respond
impact: Hib, pneumococcal and meningococcal conjugate vaccines are given to most of the world's babies and cut childhood meningitis and pneumonia deaths by millions.

name: DNA fingerprinting
how: Restriction enzymes, gel electrophoresis, DNA probes (later PCR); ★ variable repeat lengths unique to each person
impact: The standard of forensic evidence and paternity testing worldwide; national DNA databases hold tens of millions of profiles.

name: Anti-rejection drugs
how: Fungal fermentation, organic chemistry; ★ calcineurin blocking of T-cell activation (cyclosporine)
impact: Turned organ transplants from experiments into routine care; well over a million transplants since.

name: Ivermectin
how: Soil-bacterium fermentation, chemical modification; ★ paralysing nerve channels of worms and mites
impact: Hundreds of millions of doses a year in mass treatment of river blindness and elephantiasis, and the best-selling livestock drug.

name: Semiconductor laser
how: Laser, light-emitting diodes, ★ quantum-well heterojunction; first mass-produced for CD players
impact: In every optical drive, fibre-optic link, barcode scanner, laser printer and mouse; billions made each year.
why: A shrunk Laser card, but it changed who uses lasers: from labs to a cent-cheap part in billions of devices, so I'd keep it.

name: Medical abortion pill
how: Organic synthesis of a steroid; ★ progesterone-receptor blocking (mifepristone, with misoprostol)
impact: Now the most common method of abortion in many countries, used by tens of millions of women.

name: Desktop publishing
how: Personal computer, graphical user interface, laser printers, page-description language, outline fonts
impact: Ended typesetting as a trade; how newsletters, magazines, books and office documents have been laid out since.

name: Digital synthesizer and MIDI
how: Microchips, ★ FM/digital sound synthesis, a serial control protocol linking instruments and computers
impact: How almost all recorded popular music, film scores and game audio is made and sequenced.

name: Fly-by-wire airliner
how: Computers, sensors, actuators, glass-cockpit displays; flight-envelope protection in software
impact: Every new airliner since flies this way; it underpins the jump in air safety for four billion passengers a year.

name: HIV blood test
how: Radioimmune assay's successor (ELISA), viral antigens grown in cell culture
impact: Made the world's blood supply safe from HIV and made diagnosis, and hence treatment, possible for tens of millions.
why: Like the ulcer cure, an existing method (enzyme immunoassay) aimed at a new target; but blood screening is a new practice at vast scale.

name: Direct-to-home satellite TV
how: Communications satellites, small dish, low-noise block converter
impact: Hundreds of millions of homes, especially in India, Africa and rural areas, get TV by dish.
why: The Communications satellites card put in every home: it changed who receives it, so borderline rather than drop.

name: Neodymium magnet
how: Rare-earth magnet, powder metallurgy; neodymium-iron-boron alloy
impact: The strongest cheap magnet: in every hard drive, phone speaker, EV motor and wind-turbine generator.
why: A cheaper, stronger version of the Rare-earth magnet card; it made those magnets mass-market, so borderline.

name: Active-matrix LCD
how: Liquid crystal display, ★ thin-film transistors printed on glass, one per pixel
impact: Made the flat colour screens of laptops, phones and TVs; billions of panels a year.
why: A version of the LCD card; the per-pixel transistor changed it from calculator digits to every screen, so borderline.

name: Microcredit
how: Group lending, savings and loan ledgers; ★ peer liability in place of collateral
impact: Over 100 million borrowers, mostly poor women, get small loans this way.
why: Is it an invention or a business? It's a lending method like container shipping is a logistics one.

name: Home blood-glucose meter
how: Rapid test strip, enzyme (glucose oxidase) reaction, photometer or electrode, microchips
impact: Hundreds of millions of diabetics test their own blood daily; it made tight insulin control possible.
why: Sits between the Rapid test strip and CGM cards; I'd keep it as the device that put lab testing in the home.

name: Word processor software
how: Personal computer, keyboard, screen, printer; editable text in memory
impact: Replaced the typewriter in every office and home; how most of the world's documents are written.
why: Big and everyday, but dating is fuzzy: dedicated machines and WordStar are 1970s, mass adoption 1980s.

name: Polar fleece
how: Polyester fibre (often recycled PET), napped knit; developed 1979, first garments 1981
impact: An everyday warm fabric worn by hundreds of millions, often made from plastic bottles.
why: Everyday clothing like spandex; first fleece cloth was 1979 but the widely used product dates from 1981.

name: Camcorder
how: Video tape recorder, CCD image sensor, camera; recorder and camera in one handheld body
impact: Put home video in tens of millions of families' hands; now absorbed into phones.
why: The VCR shrunk and joined to a camera; changed who could make video, but phones have since replaced it.

name: Geographic information system
how: Computers, digitised maps, database; layered spatial data
impact: The standard way cities, utilities, farms and armies plan by map.
why: The standard way planners work, but mostly invisible to the public.

name: Computer-generated imagery
how: Computers, ★ 3D rendering with light simulation, frame buffers
impact: Every blockbuster, animated film and video game now runs on it.
why: Widely used only from about 1989-95; 1982 marks the first feature-film use.

name: Insulin pen
how: Insulin, disposable syringe, cartridge, dial mechanism
impact: Now the main way tens of millions inject insulin.
why: A version of the syringe that changed how diabetics inject; borderline under m4.

name: Shock-wave lithotripsy
how: Spark discharge, ellipsoidal reflector, X-ray or ultrasound aiming; ★ focused shock waves shattering stones
impact: Ended open surgery for most kidney stones; millions treated.
why: Standard care, but for one condition; on the fence between field-standard and niche.

name: Engine control computer
how: Microchips, ★ oxygen sensor feedback, electronic fuel injection, catalytic converter
impact: In every one of the world's 1.5 billion cars; it made clean, efficient engines possible.
why: Hidden part of the car rather than something people use directly; I'd lean keep.

name: Rolling suitcase
how: Wheel and axle, telescoping handle, luggage; two-wheel tilt design
impact: Pulled by most of the world's air travellers.
why: Everyday travel object (like the zipper), not a lab item; simple but universal.

name: Variable-speed motor drive
how: Electric motors, ★ insulated-gate bipolar transistor switching, pulse-width modulation
impact: Runs trains, EVs, lifts, heat pumps and factory motors, saving a large share of industrial electricity.
why: Hidden component, though everything electric that moves now runs through one.

name: Implantable defibrillator
how: Defibrillator, pacemaker, lithium battery, sensing electronics
impact: Over a million people carry one against sudden cardiac death.
why: Just below the cut; also the Defibrillator card put inside the body (an m4 borderline otherwise).

name: Superabsorbent diaper
how: Disposable diaper, ★ superabsorbent polymer gel that holds hundreds of times its weight
impact: Made diapers thin and dry; billions used a day, plus sanitary pads.
why: Below the decade's cut, and largely a version of the Disposable diaper card.

name: Sticky notes
how: Paper, ★ low-tack microsphere adhesive
impact: A staple of offices worldwide.
why: A niche convenience like hook-and-loop.

name: Acyclovir
how: Organic synthesis; ★ a drug activated only by viral enzymes
impact: The first safe antiviral, for herpes and shingles; template for later antivirals.
why: Below the decade's cut; its legacy lives in the Antiretroviral HIV therapy card.

name: Clot-busting drugs
how: Recombinant protein drugs (tPA), intravenous infusion
impact: Standard emergency treatment for heart attack and stroke.
why: Below the cut, and covered by the Recombinant protein drugs card.

name: Horizontal drilling
how: Oil wells, downhole mud motors, steerable bits, measurement while drilling
impact: Paired with fracking it unlocked shale oil and gas.
why: Covered by the Fracking card it made possible.

name: Low-power RISC processor
how: Microchips; simplified instruction set
impact: In nearly every phone and embedded device.
why: A version of the Microchips card doing the same job for the same people.

name: Contraceptive implant
how: Oral contraceptives' hormones, silicone capsules, slow release
impact: Tens of millions of women use long-acting implants or injections.
why: Below the decade's cut.

name: Chip card
how: Credit card, microchips; tamper-resistant secure chip
impact: Billions of bank and SIM cards carry one.
why: A version of the Credit card card; the Contactless card already covers the chip-card line.

name: Low-calorie sweetener (aspartame)
how: Organic synthesis of a dipeptide
impact: In diet drinks drunk by hundreds of millions.
why: Same job, same way, same people as the Saccharin card.

name: Disposable contact lenses
how: Contact lenses, molded hydrogel
impact: Most of the 140 million lens wearers use them.
why: A version of the Contact lenses card.

name: Compact fluorescent lamp
how: ★ Gas-discharge fluorescence (no fluorescent card on the board), folded tube, electronic ballast
impact: Billions sold 1990-2015 before white LEDs replaced them.
why: Below the cut and now superseded by White LED lighting; but note the fluorescent tube itself (1938) seems missing from the board.

name: AZT (first HIV drug)
how: Organic synthesis; reverse-transcriptase inhibitor
impact: First drug to slow AIDS.
why: Superseded by the Antiretroviral HIV therapy card.
